text:
maria: Heads up — seeing sporadic east-west packet loss between GPU nodes in us-east-2 during nightly training. P99 latency spikes and TCP retransmits, looks correlated with bursty traffic from model checkpoints.

alex: Details? which nodes and how often are you seeing this?

maria: Affected subset is ~4/120 nodes in gpu-pool-a (node-197, node-203, node-211, node-214). Happens ~2-3 times per night window, lasts ~30–90s. tcpdump shows gaps on VXLAN encapsulated traffic, example: 

```
15:04:27.123456 vxlan0 > eth0: IP 10.10.12.34 > 10.10.45.67: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12945, ack 54321, win 65535, length 600
15:04:27.223789 IP 10.10.12.34 > 10.10.45.67: Flags [P.], seq 12945:13545, ack 54321, win 65535, length 600 (retransmission)
```

Looks like retransmits on the overlay, not just application.

jay: Any recent CNI or kernel/driver changes?

maria: We bumped kernel on those hosts to 6.2.x and upgraded the mlx5 firmware/driver last week for RDMA perf. No CNI change. MTU values look suspicious too — host eth mtu 1500, vxlan mtu 1450 on some nodes, but overlay MTU reported 1420 on others.

tim: We did a kernel/driver rollout on 2025-11-02 for RDMA tuning. There's a known interaction between mlx5 offloads and VXLAN in some kernels. Could be GRO/GSO issues.

maria: I ran quick throughput tests. iperf3 between two affected nodes with burst load causes transient packet loss and lots of retransmits. tracepath shows PMTU 1450.

netops-bot: Created incident INC-4021 for intermittent vxlan packet loss in us-east-2. Assigned to alex.

alex: Can you try reproducing with DF (don't fragment) to rule out fragmentation versus offload artifacts? e.g.

```
ping -s 1400 -M do <pod-ip>
```

maria: Ran that — ~5/10 lost with DF, but with DF disabled pings pass. That points at fragmentation or a host-side offload mismatch.

jay: Try disabling GRO/GSO/TSO on host NIC and overlay interface on a test node:

```
# on host
ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off
# and for the vxlan device
ethtool -K vxlan0 gro off gso off tso off
```

maria: Did that on node-197 and node-203, re-ran iperf/ping under burst. Drops disappeared, p99 latency stable. CPU usage went up during bursts but no packet loss. So disabling offloads mitigates.

tim: Confirms hypothesis: interaction between mlx5 offloads + VXLAN checksums/segmentation in kernel 6.2. Workaround is to disable offload on overlay interfaces or pin these pools to older kernel/driver until upstream fix.

alex: Plan of action:
1) Start a 2-node canary to disable GRO/GSO on vxlan/eth for gpu-pool-a (node-197/node-203) — owner: alex, ETA 30m for canary.
2) Collect mlx counters and kernel logs, open a driver ticket with vendor if repro is consistent — owner: maria.
3) Run fleet-wide MTU/offload audit and a synthetic east-west burst test (iperf3) across gpu pools — owner: tim, ETA 24h.
4) If canary passes, roll fix to remaining affected nodes and consider automated daemonset to apply offload toggles for this kernel version — owner: alex.

maria: Starting canary now, will monitor telemetry (p99 latency, tcp_retrans_once, ksoftirqd). :eyes:

netops-bot: canary-deploy: disable-offload/gpu-pool-a initiated on node-197, node-203

alex: If canary looks good after 1h, we expand to rest of the impacted set. Also let's ensure a rollback plan to re-enable offloads if CPU cost is unacceptable.

tim: Add regression test to CI: heavy east-west burst with varying MTU and DF set to detect this in future.

maria: Collecting dmesg, mlx5 counters (``mlx5stats``) and will attach diagnostics to INC-4021. Will post results in this thread.

alex: Thanks — keep updates short in thread. If anyone sees new occurrences on other pools, ping me directly. :thumbsup:
